title: Surds and rationalising
intro: Read this before the surd questions.

blocks.title: what a surd is
blocks.body: A surd is a root that cannot be written as a whole number or a fraction, like $\sqrt2\approx1.414$. It is best left as $\sqrt2$ because the decimal is never exact.

blocks.title: the surd rules
items: $(a+b)(a-b)=a^{2}-b^{2}$, so a conjugate removes the root

blocks.body: To rationalise $\dfrac{c}{a+b\sqrt n}$ multiply top and bottom by the **conjugate** $a-b\sqrt n$. For $\dfrac{c}{a-b\sqrt n}$ use $a+b\sqrt n$.

blocks.title: watch the roots of sums
items: Only like surds add: $5\sqrt6+4\sqrt6=9\sqrt6$, but $\sqrt2+\sqrt3$ stays as it is.

blocks.title: typed answers
blocks.body: Write roots as `sqrt(2)`. Rationalised answers must have no root in the denominator.
